title: Sequential Stack — Practitioner's Workshop Flow
description: A plain-field, white-base layout where numbered step boxes march horizontally as a scannable process diagram, built for live hands-on instruction. Inline monospace snippets and a cyan-to-blue section banner anchor each module without competing with the content.
philosophy: This template exists for practitioners teaching practitioners — it trusts the numbered horizontal sequence to carry all visual weight and refuses to decorate around it. Texture, background motifs, and gradient fields are stripped away so learners with laptops open can parse the step flow in a single glance. Code is a first-class citizen: mono snippets sit inline without apology or special callout boxes. It is engineered for the workshop room, not the auditorium or the boardroom.
goodFor: Live coding workshops with 4–8 clearly sequenced steps
Hands-on tutorials where learners follow along in real time
Developer bootcamp and curriculum-style instruction decks
Bilingual technical sessions with English-leading code terms and inline one-liners
avoidFor: Keynote-style abstract concept talks with no sequential process
Chart-heavy data reviews requiring dense grid layouts
Brand-forward product launches or marketing presentations
Slides relying on background imagery or decorative surface motifs
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The cover reads like a workshop whiteboard wiped clean and waiting — the single horizontal banner at top acts as a chalkboard rail: functional, authoritative, undecorated. Below it, the white field breathes with deliberate emptiness so the title lands as an instruction rather than a headline. Visual weight concentrates at the banner-to-white seam; all text below aligns left and reads as a practitioner's briefing, not a product reveal. Avoid softening motifs, decorative gradients, or any surface texture — the slide should feel as comfortable projected in a seminar room as rendered in a terminal.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-width cyan-to-blue horizontal banner occupies roughly the top fifth of the slide as the sole structural anchor; the remaining white field below is open and uninterrupted. Title sits flush-left at the vertical midpoint of the white area, with a session descriptor or subtitle indented one logical level beneath it. A 6% uniform outer margin frames all four edges; a small module label or step-count token is tucked inside the right end of the banner. No footer band on the title slide — the bottom edge is intentionally clear.

examples.promptCore: A digital workshop whiteboard — clinical white field, zero ornament, total clarity. The horizontal step row should feel like a precision-printed instruction sheet: evenly paced, left-to-right scannable in one glance without visual warm-up. Inline code fragments sit inside their step cells with the same visual weight as the action labels, never isolated or spotlit, reinforcing that code is content, not commentary. The section banner at the top edge carries quiet module authority — a cool gradient stripe that orients without competing with the sequential diagram below.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column white-base canvas with ~6% outer margins; a full-width, edge-to-edge cyan-to-blue section banner spans the top ~12% of slide height, holding the module label flush-left. Below it, a horizontal row of 4–6 equally-spaced numbered step boxes occupies the vertical center of the remaining canvas across cols 1–12, each box stacking a large step numeral, a short action label, and an inline monospace code snippet. Thin hairline connector rules thread through box midpoints to telegraph sequence; slide index is anchored bottom-right with no competing footer band.
